q: An 'assessment delivery' of a consignment at the destination station is granted where:

options.A: The Railway Receipt for the consignment has been lost
options.B: The consignment is of a perishable nature
options.C: The consignment is to be delivered at a station short of its destination
options.D: The consignee desires delivery after an assessment of the extent of damage or shortage in the consignment

e: Assessment delivery is granted where the consignee desires delivery of the consignment after an assessment of the extent of damage or shortage in it.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Freight charges on consignments of a perishable nature are required to be prepaid at the time of booking.
2. Perishable consignments can be booked on 'to-pay' terms in the same manner as ordinary goods traffic.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: freight on consignments of a perishable nature must be prepaid at the time of booking; such consignments cannot be booked on to-pay terms.

q: Explosives offered for carriage by rail are accepted:

options.A: Only by goods trains, subject to the conditions laid down in the Red Tariff
options.B: By passenger trains, if loaded in the guard's brake van
options.C: By any train, without any special conditions
options.D: Only in unreserved coaches of passenger trains

e: Explosives are accepted for carriage only by goods trains, subject to the conditions laid down in the Red Tariff.

q: The Advice of Internal Check in respect of the accounts of a station is issued by the Traffic Accounts Office:

options.A: Every week, after the weekly check of station returns
options.B: Every month, after the check of the station's monthly balance sheet and returns
options.C: Once a year, at the close of the financial year
options.D: Only in a month in which an inspection of the station is carried out

e: The Advice of Internal Check is issued by the Traffic Accounts Office every month, after the check of the station's monthly balance sheet and returns.

q: During his inspection of a station, the Travelling Inspector of Accounts ordinarily exercises:

options.A: A complete check of the accounts of one selected month and a test check of the accounts of the other months
options.B: No check of accounts, his inspection being confined to the verification of cash
options.C: A complete check of the accounts of all the twelve months since the last inspection
options.D: A check only of the goods accounts, the coaching accounts being excluded

e: During a station inspection, the Travelling Inspector of Accounts ordinarily makes a complete check of the accounts of one selected month and a test check of the other months.

q: During a month, the goods locomotives of a railway consumed 7,200 litres of diesel oil and performed 18,00,000 Gross Tonne Kilometres. The Specific Fuel Consumption (SFC) of the railway for the month is:

options.A: 0.4 litres per 1000 GTKM
options.B: 4.0 litres per 1000 GTKM
options.C: 40.0 litres per 1000 GTKM
options.D: 2.5 litres per 1000 GTKM

e: SFC = fuel consumed / GTKM performed x 1000 = 7,200 / 18,00,000 x 1000 = 4.0 litres per 1000 GTKM.

q: Consignments of currency notes and other valuables (treasure) tendered by Government or the Reserve Bank of India are carried by the Railways:

options.A: In special treasure vans/coaches, under proper escort and on payment of the prescribed charges
options.B: In ordinary parcel vans, along with other parcels
options.C: Only by road, under railway escort
options.D: Free of charge, as departmental traffic

e: Consignments of currency notes and valuables (treasure) tendered by Government or the Reserve Bank are carried in special treasure vans or coaches, under proper escort and on payment of the prescribed charges.

q: Empty packages, such as drums, cylinders and gunny bags, which had earlier been carried by rail as the packing of goods and are returned by the consignee, are carried by the Railways:

options.A: At the same rates as the loaded packages
options.B: Only when loaded in passenger trains
options.C: Free of charge in all cases
options.D: At concessional (reduced) freight rates, subject to the prescribed conditions

e: Empty packages such as drums, cylinders and gunny bags, returned after earlier carriage as packing of goods, are carried at concessional (reduced) freight rates subject to the prescribed conditions.

q: Concession in rail fares for travel in connection with medical treatment is admissible, under the prescribed conditions, to:

options.A: Thalassemia major and haemophilia patients travelling for treatment or periodic check-up
options.B: All patients suffering from any ailment whatsoever
options.C: Only patients referred by a Government hospital
options.D: Only children below twelve years of age

e: Fare concession for medical treatment is admissible, under the prescribed conditions, to thalassemia major and haemophilia patients travelling for treatment or periodic check-up.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The free time allowed for the loading or unloading of a wagon is reckoned from the time the wagon is placed at the loading or unloading point for that purpose.
2. The free time is reckoned from the time the train carrying the wagon arrives in the station yard.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: the free time for loading or unloading is reckoned from the time the wagon is placed at the loading or unloading point, not from the arrival of the train in the yard.

q: Parcels which are not taken delivery of by the consignees within the free time allowed after their arrival at the destination station are liable to:

options.A: Be destroyed by the Railways without any notice
options.B: Be returned to the booking station at the cost of the Railways
options.C: Wharfage charges for the period for which they remain on the station premises
options.D: A penalty equal to the parcel charges in every case

e: Parcels not taken delivery of within the free time after arrival at destination are liable to wharfage charges for the period they remain on the station premises.

q: Charges for depositing luggage in the cloak room at a station are levied:

options.A: Per package, irrespective of the period for which it remains deposited
options.B: Per kilogram of the luggage, per day
options.C: Per package, for each period of 24 hours or part thereof
options.D: As a percentage of the value of the luggage deposited

e: Cloak room charges for depositing luggage are levied per package for each period of 24 hours or part thereof.

q: The correctness of the distance for which freight has been charged on a goods invoice is verified in the Traffic Accounts Office with reference to:

options.A: The distance declared by the consignor in the Forwarding Note
options.B: The route map displayed in the goods shed
options.C: The statement of the guard of the train which carried the consignment
options.D: The Local Distance Tables and the Junction Distance Tables in force

e: The correctness of the distance charged on a goods invoice is verified in the Traffic Accounts Office with reference to the Local Distance Tables and the Junction Distance Tables in force.

q: Students travelling in a group on an educational tour sponsored by a recognised educational institution are entitled to:

options.A: Free travel in all classes of trains
options.B: Concession only in the unreserved classes
options.C: No concession of any kind
options.D: Concession in rail fares, on production of the prescribed concession certificate/form from the institution

e: Students travelling in a group on an educational tour sponsored by a recognised institution are entitled to fare concession on production of the prescribed concession certificate or form from the institution.

q: Under Section 167 of the Railways Act, 1989, a person is prohibited from smoking in a compartment of a train where:

options.A: The train is standing at a station
options.B: The compartment is an air-conditioned coach
options.C: Any other passenger in the compartment objects to the smoking
options.D: The ticket checking staff is present in the coach

e: Under Section 167 of the Railways Act, smoking in a train compartment is prohibited where any other passenger in the compartment objects to it.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A passenger may carry his personal luggage, within the free allowance admissible to him, in the compartment itself, subject to the prescribed limits of size.
2. Luggage in excess of the free allowance can also be carried in the compartment free of charge, without being booked.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: personal luggage within the free allowance may be carried in the compartment subject to size limits, but excess luggage cannot be carried there free without being booked.

q: The 'Own Your Wagon Scheme' (OYWS) of Indian Railways enabled:

options.A: Passengers to own reserved coaches for their journeys
options.B: Bulk consumers and industries to own wagons, which were operated by the Railways, so as to ensure assured supply of wagons for their traffic
options.C: Private parties to run their own goods trains on the railway network
options.D: Station Masters to hire wagons locally from private parties

e: The Own Your Wagon Scheme enabled bulk consumers and industries to own wagons, operated by the Railways, so as to ensure assured wagon supply for their traffic.

q: The travel insurance facility offered to passengers booking tickets online (e-tickets) primarily covers, subject to the terms of the policy:

options.A: Loss of the passenger's luggage after completion of the journey
options.B: Loss suffered on account of delay in the departure of trains
options.C: Damage to the passenger's property at his residence
options.D: Accidental death of, or injury to, the passenger during the course of the journey

e: The travel insurance offered with online ticket booking covers, subject to the policy terms, accidental death of or injury to the passenger during the course of the journey.

q: Commodities offered for booking as goods traffic are required to comply with:

options.A: The standard packing conditions prescribed for them in the Goods Tariff
options.B: The packing suggested by the trade association of the consignor
options.C: No packing conditions, where the goods are booked at railway risk
options.D: The packing conditions prescribed for parcel traffic only

e: Commodities offered for booking as goods traffic must comply with the standard packing conditions prescribed for them in the Goods Tariff.

q: Where live animals are booked for carriage by rail, the responsibility for feeding and watering them during the journey rests with:

options.A: The station staff at the destination station
options.B: The guard of the train
options.C: The attendant deputed by the consignor, who accompanies the animals
options.D: The Traffic Accounts Office

e: Where live animals are carried, feeding and watering them during the journey is the responsibility of the attendant deputed by the consignor, who accompanies the animals.

q: In railway statistics, one 'traffic unit' represents:

options.A: One train kilometre performed
options.B: One passenger kilometre or one net tonne kilometre of goods traffic
options.C: One wagon day on line
options.D: One route kilometre worked for one day

e: In railway statistics, one traffic unit represents one passenger kilometre or one net tonne kilometre of goods traffic, the common unit combining coaching and goods output.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Advice of Internal Check conveys to the station the consolidated result - the debits and credits - of the internal check of its accounts for the month.
2. Error sheets communicate to the station the individual errors and discrepancies detected in its accounts, for explanation and compliance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the Advice of Internal Check conveys the consolidated debits and credits of the month's check, while error sheets communicate the individual errors for explanation and compliance.

q: Wharfage charges are also leviable in respect of:

options.A: Wagons detained at a station beyond the free time allowed for unloading
options.B: Goods brought into a goods shed for booking but kept there beyond the free time allowed, without being loaded
options.C: Luggage deposited in the cloak room of a station
options.D: Coaching vehicles stabled in the station yard

e: Wharfage is also leviable on goods brought into a goods shed for booking but kept there beyond the free time allowed, without being loaded.

q: A railway performed 24,00,000 Net Tonne Kilometres during a period in which the goods engine days numbered 600. The Net Tonne Kilometres per engine day are:
e: Net Tonne Kilometres per engine day = NTKM performed / goods engine days = 24,00,000 / 600 = 4,000.

q: Locomotives, coaches and other vehicles which are moved over the Railways on their own wheels, instead of being loaded on wagons, are charged:

options.A: Conveyance charges per vehicle, based on the distance for which they are hauled or run
options.B: The same freight as a full wagonload of the highest-rated commodity
options.C: No charges at all, in every case
options.D: Parcel charges at the highest scale

e: Vehicles moved over the Railways on their own wheels, instead of being loaded on wagons, are charged conveyance charges per vehicle based on the distance hauled or run.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Compensation for the death of, or injury to, a passenger in a train accident, such as a collision or derailment of a train carrying passengers, is payable under Section 124 of the Railways Act, 1989.
2. Compensation for the death of, or injury to, a passenger in an 'untoward incident' is payable under Section 124A of the Railways Act, 1989, on the principle of no-fault liability.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: Section 124 covers compensation for death or injury in a train accident, and Section 124A covers untoward incidents on the no-fault liability principle.

q: Where a rationalised route has been notified for a stream of goods traffic, the freight on that traffic is charged on the basis of the distance by:

options.A: The shortest route between the forwarding and destination stations
options.B: The rationalised route so notified, even though it is longer than the shortest route
options.C: The route specified by the consignor in the Forwarding Note
options.D: The route over which the railway actually earns the least

e: Where a rationalised route is notified for a stream of traffic, freight is charged on the distance by that route, even though it is longer than the shortest route.

q: In the case of Tatkal tickets, the position regarding concessions in fare is that:

options.A: No concession is admissible on Tatkal tickets
options.B: All concessions admissible on ordinary tickets are also admissible on Tatkal tickets
options.C: Concession is admissible only to students on Tatkal tickets
options.D: Concession is admissible only to senior citizens on Tatkal tickets

e: No concession of any kind is admissible on Tatkal tickets; the full fare including Tatkal charges is payable by all passengers.

q: Under the Premium Tatkal scheme, the correct position regarding the accommodation allotted is that:

options.A: Waitlisted and RAC tickets are issued in the same manner as under the ordinary Tatkal scheme
options.B: Only RAC accommodation is allotted and no confirmed berths are given
options.C: Only waitlisted tickets are issued, which are confirmed later against cancellations
options.D: Only confirmed accommodation is allotted and no RAC or waitlisted tickets are issued

e: Under Premium Tatkal, only confirmed accommodation is allotted; no RAC or waitlisted tickets are issued under the scheme.

q: A passenger holding a waitlisted ticket issued at a computerised reservation counter (paper ticket) is:

options.A: Treated as travelling without a ticket if he boards the train
options.B: Not permitted to enter the reserved coach of the train
options.C: Permitted to board and travel in the reserved coach of the train
options.D: Required to surrender the ticket at the station before the train departs

e: A waitlisted ticket issued at a computerised reservation counter (paper ticket) permits the holder to board and travel in the reserved coach of the train.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where an e-ticket is partially confirmed or in RAC after preparation of the chart, it is not cancelled automatically and the waitlisted passengers named on it may also travel.
2. Where all the passengers on an e-ticket remain waitlisted after preparation of the chart, the ticket is automatically cancelled and the fare is refunded.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a partially confirmed or RAC e-ticket is not auto-cancelled and its waitlisted passengers may travel, but a fully waitlisted e-ticket is automatically cancelled after charting with refund.

q: Where the air-conditioning equipment of an AC coach fails during the journey and the passengers are made to travel in a non-AC class, the passengers are entitled to:

options.A: Refund of the full fare paid by them
options.B: Refund of the difference between the AC class fare and the corresponding non-AC class fare, on the basis of the certificate issued by the ticket checking staff
options.C: No refund of any kind
options.D: Refund of the reservation charge only

e: Where AC equipment fails and passengers travel in a non-AC class, they are entitled to refund of the difference between the AC and corresponding non-AC fares, on the certificate of the ticket checking staff.

q: The 'Complimentary Card Pass' facility, which entitles the holder to free travel in air-conditioned classes along with a companion, is extended to:

options.A: Recipients of the Chakra series of gallantry awards
options.B: Accredited press correspondents
options.C: Season ticket holders
options.D: Sports persons participating in national tournaments

e: The Complimentary Card Pass, entitling free travel in air-conditioned classes with a companion, is extended to recipients of the Chakra series of gallantry awards.

q: Concession in railway fares is admissible, under the prescribed conditions, to:

options.A: Persons travelling for a routine medical check-up for any ailment
options.B: Patients suffering from minor ailments travelling to a hospital
options.C: Attendants accompanying any patient travelling by train
options.D: Cancer patients travelling for treatment or periodic check-up

e: Fare concession is admissible, under the prescribed conditions, to sports persons travelling to participate in tournaments at the national or State level.

q: Concession in railway fares is admissible, under the prescribed conditions, to:

options.A: All patients travelling to any hospital for indoor treatment
options.B: Kidney patients travelling for dialysis treatment
options.C: Persons accompanying a patient as attendant, in all cases
options.D: Patients travelling for a general health check-up

e: Fare concession is admissible, under the prescribed conditions, to sports persons travelling to participate in tournaments at the national or State level.

q: The concession in fare admissible to Divyangjan passengers (such as the orthopaedically handicapped and the visually impaired) is available:

options.A: Only in the unreserved classes
options.B: Only in the Sleeper class
options.C: In all classes, including the air-conditioned classes
options.D: Only in Rajdhani Express trains

e: The concession admissible to Divyangjan passengers is available in all classes of travel, including the air-conditioned classes.

q: Concession in railway fares is admissible, under the prescribed conditions, to:

options.A: Sports persons travelling to participate in tournaments at the national or State level
options.B: Spectators travelling to witness sporting events
options.C: Owners of sports goods firms travelling on business
options.D: Retired sports persons travelling for personal purposes

e: Fare concession is admissible, under the prescribed conditions, to sports persons travelling to participate in tournaments at the national or State level.

q: The cost of maintenance of a private siding on the Railways is borne by:

options.A: The Railways, as part of their ordinary working expenses
options.B: The Railways and the siding owner in equal shares in all cases
options.C: The Traffic Accounts Office of the zonal railway
options.D: The siding owner, at whose cost the siding is maintained

e: The cost of maintenance of a private siding is borne by the siding owner, at whose cost the siding is maintained.

q: 'Running track kilometres' of a railway represent:

options.A: The route kilometres of the railway, including the sidings and yard lines
options.B: The aggregate length of all the running lines of the railway, each line being counted separately and sidings and yard lines being excluded
options.C: The length of double-line sections only
options.D: The length of electrified lines only

e: Running track kilometres are the aggregate length of all the running lines of a railway, each line counted separately, with sidings and yard lines excluded.

q: The Railway Mail Service (RMS), which handles the mail carried by trains, functions under:

options.A: The Department of Posts
options.B: The Commercial Department of the Railways
options.C: IRCTC
options.D: A private courier consortium engaged by the Railways

e: The Railway Mail Service, which handles mail carried by trains, functions under the Department of Posts, not the Railways' Commercial Department.

q: The PNR (Passenger Name Record) number allotted to a reservation on Indian Railways is a:

options.A: 6-digit number
options.B: 8-digit number
options.C: 10-digit number
options.D: 12-digit number

e: The PNR number allotted to a reservation is a 10-digit number, which uniquely identifies the booking and is used to check reservation status.

q: The in-built wallet facility provided in the 'UTS on Mobile' application of Indian Railways is known as:

options.A: Rail Wallet Pro
options.B: UTS Wallet Plus
options.C: e-Wallet Rail
options.D: R-Wallet

e: The in-built wallet facility of the UTS on Mobile application is known as R-Wallet, usable for booking unreserved tickets through the application.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation IRCTC stands for:

options.A: Indian Railway Catering and Transport Corporation
options.B: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation
options.C: International Rail Catering and Tourism Company
options.D: Indian Rail Coach and Tourism Corporation

e: IRCTC stands for Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation, the railway undertaking handling catering, tourism and online ticketing.

q: 'Earnings per traffic unit' of a railway are computed as:

options.A: The gross earnings of the railway divided by the total traffic units performed by it
options.B: The Net Tonne Kilometres divided by the passenger kilometres
options.C: The gross earnings divided by the route kilometres open for traffic
options.D: The gross earnings divided by the train kilometres run

e: Earnings per traffic unit = gross earnings / total traffic units performed, giving the average earning from one passenger kilometre or net tonne kilometre.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Specific Fuel Consumption is worked out separately for the passenger (coaching) services and for the goods services.
2. Specific Energy Consumption is the corresponding index of energy consumption used in electric traction.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: Specific Fuel Consumption is worked out separately for passenger and goods services, and Specific Energy Consumption is the corresponding index used in electric traction.

q: In Garib Rath Express trains, the position regarding supply of bedding to the passengers is that:

options.A: Bedding is not provided in these trains at all
options.B: Bedding is provided free of charge to all passengers
options.C: Bedding is provided to the passengers on payment of the prescribed charges
options.D: Bedding is provided only to passengers travelling in the air-conditioned chair car

e: In Garib Rath Express trains, bedding is provided to passengers on payment of the prescribed charges; it is neither free nor entirely absent.

q: Antyodaya Express trains of Indian Railways are:

options.A: Fully air-conditioned trains with dynamic fares
options.B: Trains having only Sleeper class accommodation
options.C: Trains run exclusively for the carriage of parcels
options.D: Fully unreserved trains having general second class accommodation

e: Antyodaya Express trains are superfast services composed entirely of unreserved general second-class coaches, intended for the benefit of the common passenger.

q: Humsafar Express trains of Indian Railways are:

options.A: Fully air-conditioned trains having only AC 3-tier accommodation
options.B: Fully unreserved trains for short-distance travel
options.C: Trains having only air-conditioned chair car accommodation
options.D: Trains having a mixture of AC and non-AC classes

e: Humsafar Express trains are fully air-conditioned trains having only AC 3-tier accommodation.

q: The quota of reserved accommodation earmarked in trains for allotment to defence personnel travelling on duty or on warrants is known as the:

options.A: Emergency quota
options.B: Defence quota
options.C: Foreign tourist quota
options.D: Pooled quota

e: The quota of reserved accommodation earmarked for defence personnel travelling on duty or on warrants is known as the Defence quota.

q: A passenger travelling on a Circular Journey Ticket is entitled to:

options.A: Break his journey only at the destination station named on the ticket
options.B: Break his journey at any station, without any endorsement on the ticket
options.C: Break his journey at intermediate stations on the route, subject to the prescribed conditions and endorsement
options.D: Break his journey only at the station from which the ticket was issued

e: A Circular Journey Ticket holder may break journey at intermediate stations on the route, subject to the prescribed conditions and endorsement on the ticket.

q: During a month, the locomotives of a railway ran 9,60,000 engine kilometres and the engine days numbered 3,200. The engine kilometres per engine day are:
e: Engine kilometres per engine day = engine kilometres run / engine days = 9,60,000 / 3,200 = 300.

q: A railway performed 72,00,000 passenger kilometres during a period in which the seat kilometres offered were 90,00,000. The load factor (occupation ratio) of the coaching services is:
e: Load factor = passenger kilometres / seat kilometres offered x 100 = 72,00,000 / 90,00,000 x 100 = 80%.

q: The Gross Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway during a year were 1,20,00,000 and the route kilometres open for traffic were 4,000. The density of goods traffic on the railway is:

options.A: 2,500 GTKM per route kilometre
options.B: 3,000 GTKM per route kilometre
options.C: 3,500 GTKM per route kilometre
options.D: 4,000 GTKM per route kilometre

e: Density of goods traffic = GTKM performed / route kilometres = 1,20,00,000 / 4,000 = 3,000 GTKM per route kilometre.

q: During a period, the total wagon kilometres run on a railway were 1,50,00,000, of which the empty wagon kilometres were 45,00,000. The percentage of empty wagon kilometres to total wagon kilometres is:
e: Percentage of empty wagon kilometres = 45,00,000 / 1,50,00,000 x 100 = 30%.

q: The total cost of the goods services of a railway for a period is Rs 54,00,000 and the Net Tonne Kilometres performed are 18,00,000. The cost per Net Tonne Kilometre is:
e: Cost per Net Tonne Kilometre = total cost of goods services / NTKM performed = Rs 54,00,000 / 18,00,000 = Rs 3.00.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The train hours used in computing the average speed of trains include the time of halts at the intermediate stations en route.
2. The time spent by a train at the destination terminal after its arrival is also included in the train hours of that train.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: train hours include halts at intermediate stations en route, but time spent at the destination terminal after arrival is not part of the train's hours.

q: The safety performance of a railway is commonly measured by the index of:

options.A: Train accidents per route kilometre
options.B: Train accidents per passenger carried
options.C: Engine failures per lakh engine kilometres
options.D: Train accidents per million train kilometres

e: The safety performance of a railway is commonly measured by the index of train accidents per million train kilometres run.

q: The Traffic Book of a zonal railway, showing the earnings of local and through traffic, is compiled in:

options.A: The Railway Board
options.B: The Traffic Accounts Office of the railway
options.C: The Commercial Department of the division
options.D: The Statistics cell of the Railway Board

e: The Traffic Book of a zonal railway, showing earnings of local and through traffic, is compiled in the Traffic Accounts Office of the railway.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A reserved ticket booked at a computerised reservation counter can be cancelled at the station even after preparation of the reservation chart, subject to the prescribed time limits.
2. An e-ticket cannot be cancelled after preparation of the reservation chart, and refund, where admissible, can only be claimed by filing a Ticket Deposit Receipt.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a counter ticket can be cancelled at the station even after charting within the prescribed time limits, while an e-ticket cannot be cancelled after charting and refund needs a Ticket Deposit Receipt.

q: At halt stations on the Railways, unreserved tickets are sold by:

options.A: Halt agents engaged for the purpose on a commission basis
options.B: The Station Master of the adjoining block station
options.C: Jansadharan Ticket Booking Sevaks attached to the halt
options.D: Facilitators engaged for the Automatic Ticket Vending Machines

e: At halt stations, unreserved tickets are sold by halt agents engaged for the purpose on a commission basis.

q: Articles of a dangerous or offensive nature are:

options.A: Permitted to be carried by a passenger as luggage if they are securely packed
options.B: Permitted to be carried as luggage in the brake van without any restriction
options.C: Not permitted to be carried by a passenger as luggage in the passenger compartment
options.D: Prohibited only if they are liquids

e: Articles of a dangerous or offensive nature are not permitted to be carried by a passenger as luggage in the passenger compartment.

q: Under the Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal policy, such terminals may be developed:

options.A: Only on railway land
options.B: Only on private land outside the railway boundary
options.C: Only at the major ports
options.D: On railway land or on non-railway land, with rail connectivity provided by the Railways

e: Under the Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal policy, terminals may be developed on railway land or on non-railway land, with rail connectivity provided by the Railways.

q: Receipts from the sale or licensing of grass and fruit-bearing trees standing on railway land are classified under:

options.A: Goods earnings
options.B: Sundry other earnings
options.C: Other coaching earnings
options.D: Capital receipts

e: Receipts from the sale or licensing of grass and fruit-bearing trees standing on railway land are classified under sundry other earnings.

q: 'Gross Tonne Kilometres per engine day' is an index which measures:

options.A: The gross hauling output obtained per locomotive day
options.B: The fuel efficiency of locomotives
options.C: The utilisation of wagons in terms of distance run
options.D: The occupation of the line by trains

e: Gross Tonne Kilometres per engine day measures the gross hauling output obtained per locomotive day.

q: The reservation charge levied on a reserved ticket:

options.A: Is uniform for all classes of travel
options.B: Is levied only on tickets in the air-conditioned classes
options.C: Varies according to the class of travel
options.D: Is levied only on Tatkal tickets

e: The reservation charge levied on a reserved ticket varies according to the class of travel; it is neither uniform for all classes nor confined to AC classes or Tatkal tickets.

q: The electrical energy consumed on a railway is accounted for separately as:

options.A: Traction consumption only, non-traction consumption being ignored
options.B: A single combined figure for all purposes
options.C: Non-traction consumption only
options.D: Traction consumption and non-traction consumption

e: Electrical energy consumed on a railway is accounted for separately as traction consumption and non-traction consumption.

q: Under the Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) arrangement, the accommodation allotted to the RAC passengers is that:

options.A: Each RAC passenger is allotted a full berth for sleeping
options.B: Two RAC passengers are allotted one side-lower berth to share for sitting
options.C: RAC passengers are accommodated in the general (unreserved) coach
options.D: Each RAC passenger is allotted an upper berth

e: Under RAC, two passengers are allotted one side-lower berth to share for sitting, with berths allotted later against cancellations if available.

q: For compiling the passenger statistics, the passenger kilometres are worked out:

options.A: From the charts prepared for the reserved trains only
options.B: From the statements rendered by the guards of the trains
options.C: By estimation for all classes of tickets, whether reserved or unreserved
options.D: From the tickets issued, by multiplying the number of passengers with the distance of the journey in each case

e: Passenger kilometres are worked out from the tickets issued, by multiplying the number of passengers with the distance of the journey in each case.

q: Passenger fares for a train journey are charged on the basis of:

options.A: The shortest road distance between the two stations
options.B: The distance by the route by which the train actually travels
options.C: The straight-line (crow-fly) distance between the two stations
options.D: A uniform distance slab for all trains on the section

e: Passenger fares are charged on the basis of the distance by the route by which the train actually travels.

q: Where the loading or unloading of a consignment at a station is performed by railway labour, the position regarding the charges for such handling is that:

options.A: The handling is done free of charge in all cases
options.B: The charges are shared equally between the Railways and the party
options.C: The charges are recovered only in the case of parcel traffic
options.D: Handling charges are recovered from the consignor or the consignee, as the case may be, in addition to the freight

e: Where loading or unloading at a station is performed by railway labour, handling charges are recovered from the consignor or the consignee, as the case may be, in addition to the freight.

q: Under Section 49 of the Railways Act, 1989, a railway administration is required to exhibit at every station of the railway:

options.A: The list of employees on duty at the station
options.B: A table of the times of arrival and departure of trains and a list of fares payable for travel from the station
options.C: The annual accounts of the zonal railway
options.D: The list of licensed porters engaged at the station

e: Under Section 49 of the Railways Act, every station must exhibit a table of the times of arrival and departure of trains and a list of fares payable for travel from the station.

q: During a month, the total wagon days on a railway were 7,20,000 and the number of wagons loaded was 1,80,000. The wagon turn-round for the month is:

options.A: 3.0 days
options.B: 3.5 days
options.C: 2.5 days
options.D: 4.0 days

e: Wagon turn-round = total wagon days / wagons loaded = 7,20,000 / 1,80,000 = 4.0 days.

q: Live animals are accepted for carriage by the Railways:

options.A: Only at the railway risk rate
options.B: Only against compulsory payment of the percentage charge
options.C: Only at the owner's risk rate
options.D: Only in wagons owned by the consignor

e: Live animals are accepted for carriage by the Railways only at the owner's risk rate.

q: Where goods are booked at the owner's risk rate, the railway administration is not liable for any loss of, destruction of, damage to or non-delivery of the consignment unless:

options.A: Negligence or misconduct on the part of the Railways or of their servants is proved by the claimant
options.B: The consignment was insured by the consignor against transit risks
options.C: The consignment was carried in a sealed wagon
options.D: The value of the goods was declared at the time of booking

e: Where goods are booked at owner's risk, the Railways are not liable for loss, damage or non-delivery unless negligence or misconduct on their part is proved by the claimant.

q: A train is classified as a 'superfast' train for the purpose of levy of the superfast charge when its average speed, including halts, is not less than:

options.A: 50 kilometres per hour
options.B: 55 kilometres per hour
options.C: 60 kilometres per hour
options.D: 45 kilometres per hour

e: A train is classified as superfast for levy of the superfast charge when its average speed, including halts, is not less than 55 kilometres per hour.

q: A railway performed 36,00,000 passenger kilometres during a period in which the number of passengers carried was 90,000. The average lead of passenger traffic is:

options.A: 36 kilometres
options.B: 40 kilometres
options.C: 45 kilometres
options.D: 30 kilometres

e: Average lead of passenger traffic = passenger kilometres / passengers carried = 36,00,000 / 90,000 = 40 kilometres.

q: The functions of the erstwhile Railway Rates Tribunal, which dealt with complaints regarding the reasonableness of the rates charged by the Railways, now vest in:

options.A: The Central Administrative Tribunal
options.B: The Railway Board
options.C: The Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
options.D: The Railway Claims Tribunal

e: The functions of the erstwhile Railway Rates Tribunal, which dealt with complaints about reasonableness of rates, now vest in the Railway Claims Tribunal.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A claim for compensation for the death of, or injury to, a passenger in a train accident or an untoward incident must be filed before the Railway Claims Tribunal within one year of the occurrence of the accident or incident.
2. A claim for compensation for loss of, damage to or non-delivery of goods must be filed before the Railway Claims Tribunal within three years.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: compensation claims for death or injury in a train accident or untoward incident lie before the Railway Claims Tribunal within one year, and goods claims within three years.

q: In freight operations through the Freight Operations Information System, the abbreviation 'e-RD' stands for:

options.A: Electronic Registration of Demand
options.B: Electronic Railway Despatch
options.C: Electronic Rate Declaration
options.D: Electronic Receipt Document

e: In the Freight Operations Information System, e-RD stands for Electronic Registration of Demand, the online registration of wagon demand by freight customers.

q: The total cost of the coaching services of a railway for a period is Rs 18,00,000 and the passenger kilometres performed are 60,00,000. The cost per passenger kilometre is:
e: Cost per passenger kilometre = total cost of coaching services / passenger kilometres = Rs 18,00,000 / 60,00,000 = Rs 0.30.

q: The advance reservation period for booking reserved accommodation in trains, otherwise than under the Tatkal scheme, is:

options.A: 120 days
options.B: 90 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 60 days

e: The advance reservation period for booking reserved accommodation, otherwise than under the Tatkal scheme, is 60 days.

q: For the same class and for the same distance, the fare charged for travel by a Mail/Express train, as compared with the fare by an ordinary passenger train, is:

options.A: The same
options.B: Higher
options.C: Lower
options.D: Charged only on the return journey

e: For the same class and distance, the fare by a Mail or Express train is higher than the fare by an ordinary passenger train.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A maximum of six passengers can be booked on a single reservation requisition form.
2. Under the Tatkal scheme, a maximum of four passengers can be booked in a single PNR.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a maximum of six passengers can be booked on a single reservation requisition form, and under Tatkal a maximum of four passengers can be booked in a single PNR.

q: In connection with container traffic, the abbreviation CONCOR stands for:

options.A: Container Company of Railways
options.B: Container Corporation of India Limited
options.C: Consolidated Container Organisation
options.D: Central Container Corporation

e: CONCOR stands for Container Corporation of India Limited, the undertaking handling container traffic for the Railways.

q: A railway performed 72,00,000 passenger kilometres during a year in which the route kilometres open for traffic were 3,000. The density of passenger traffic on the railway is:

options.A: 240 passenger kilometres per route kilometre
options.B: 24,000 passenger kilometres per route kilometre
options.C: 2,000 passenger kilometres per route kilometre
options.D: 2,400 passenger kilometres per route kilometre

e: Density of passenger traffic = passenger kilometres / route kilometres = 72,00,000 / 3,000 = 2,400 passenger kilometres per route kilometre.

q: Under Section 137 of the Railways Act, 1989, the excess charge payable by a person found travelling or attempting to travel without a proper ticket is equal to the fare for the distance travelled, subject to a minimum of:

options.A: Rs 50
options.B: Rs 100
options.C: Rs 250
options.D: Rs 500

e: The minimum excess charge under the substituted Section 137 is now Rs 500 (excess charge equal to the fare, subject to a minimum of Rs 500 or the charges notified by the Central Government). (Source: Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026 (Act 8 of 2026), substituting Section 137 of the Railways Act; effective 19.06.2026.)

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A freight forwarder collects small consignments from a number of consignors and books them together as a single wagonload consignment in his own name.
2. A freight forwarder is a railway servant posted at goods sheds for canvassing traffic.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: a freight forwarder collects small consignments from many consignors and books them together as a single wagonload consignment in his own name; he is not a railway servant.

q: The goods earnings of a railway for a period are Rs 90,00,000 and the wagon days during the period are 3,00,000. The earnings per wagon day are:

options.A: Rs 3
options.B: Rs 30
options.C: Rs 300
options.D: Rs 33

e: Earnings per wagon day = goods earnings / wagon days = Rs 90,00,000 / 3,00,000 = Rs 30.

q: Before a motor cycle is accepted for booking as luggage or as a parcel, it is essential that:

options.A: It is insured against theft during transit
options.B: It is packed in a wooden crate
options.C: A security deposit is paid by the consignor
options.D: The fuel in its tank is completely drained out

e: Before a motor cycle is accepted for booking as luggage or parcel, the fuel in its tank must be completely drained out, as a safety requirement.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Busy Season Charge on goods traffic is levied at the rate of 10 per cent of the base freight rate.
2. The busy season for goods traffic is the period from October to June.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct: the busy season for goods traffic runs from October to June; the Busy Season Charge is not levied at 10 per cent of the base freight rate.

q: In the Passenger Reservation System, the abbreviation TQWL denotes:

options.A: Train Quota Wait List
options.B: Terminal Quota Wait List
options.C: Through Quota Wait List
options.D: Tatkal Quota Wait List

e: In the Passenger Reservation System, TQWL denotes the Tatkal Quota Wait List, the waitlist against the Tatkal quota.

q: During a month, the locomotives in electric traction on a railway consumed 84,000 kWh of electrical energy and performed 28,00,000 Gross Tonne Kilometres. The Specific Energy Consumption (SEC) of the railway for the month is:

options.A: 30 kWh per 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres
options.B: 3 kWh per 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres
options.C: 33 kWh per 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres
options.D: 300 kWh per 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres

e: SEC = energy consumed / GTKM performed x 1000 = 84,000 / 28,00,000 x 1000 = 30 kWh per 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Articles left behind by passengers in trains or at stations are deposited in the Lost Property Office of the Railways.
2. Articles remaining unclaimed in the Lost Property Office are handed over free of charge to the person who found them.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: articles left behind by passengers are deposited in the Lost Property Office, but unclaimed articles are not handed over free of charge to the finder.

q:
Consider the following statements about waitlists in the Passenger Reservation System:
1. The Pooled Quota Wait List (PQWL) applies to passengers boarding at stations which share a common pooled quota for the train.
2. The Remote Location Wait List (RLWL) applies to passengers boarding at important intermediate stations for which a separate quota is allotted.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the Pooled Quota Wait List covers passengers boarding at stations sharing a common pooled quota, and the Remote Location Wait List covers important intermediate stations with a separate quota.

q: A railway performed 54,00,000 passenger kilometres during a period in which the passenger train kilometres run were 12,000. The average number of passengers carried per train is:
e: Average number of passengers carried per train = passenger kilometres / passenger train kilometres = 54,00,000 / 12,000 = 450.

q: Where a reserved ticket is mutilated or torn, a refund at the station is admissible if:

options.A: The passenger files a Ticket Deposit Receipt in all such cases
options.B: The particulars of the ticket, such as the ticket number and the PNR number, are clearly legible
options.C: The passenger pays a duplicate ticket charge
options.D: The reservation chart of the train has not been prepared

e: Refund on a mutilated or torn reserved ticket is admissible at the station if the particulars of the ticket, such as the ticket number and PNR number, are clearly legible.

q: Reserved accommodation under the Foreign Tourist Quota can be booked by foreign tourists up to:

options.A: 60 days in advance of the journey
options.B: 120 days in advance of the journey
options.C: 365 days in advance of the journey
options.D: 30 days in advance of the journey

e: Reserved accommodation under the Foreign Tourist Quota can be booked by foreign tourists up to 365 days in advance of the journey.

q: The gross earnings of a railway for a year are Rs 3,000 crore and its working expenses are Rs 2,700 crore. The Operating Ratio of the railway is:

options.A: 9 per cent
options.B: 90 per cent
options.C: 111 per cent
options.D: 95 per cent

e: Operating Ratio = working expenses / gross earnings x 100 = Rs 2,700 crore / Rs 3,000 crore x 100 = 90 per cent.

q: Under the Premium Indent Scheme of the Railways, a freight customer can obtain:

options.A: Wagons on a priority or out-of-turn basis, on payment of a premium over the normal wagon registration fee
options.B: A rebate in freight for loading traffic in the empty-flow direction
options.C: Exemption from demurrage at goods terminals
options.D: Free weighment of all his consignments

e: Under the Premium Indent Scheme, a freight customer can obtain wagons on a priority or out-of-turn basis on payment of a premium over the normal wagon registration fee.

q: A paperless platform ticket can be booked by a passenger through:

options.A: The IRCTC website only
options.B: The UTS mobile application
options.C: The NTES application only
options.D: The Rail Madad portal

e: A paperless platform ticket can be booked by a passenger through the UTS mobile application.
